newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CCT Telecom to issue convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: CCT Telecom to issue convertible bonds.

text.p: CCT Telecom Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to issue HK$86.4 million in convertible bonds (CBs) maturing in 1999 for general working capital.
CCT, a telecommunications equipment maker, said Nation Unite Assets Ltd and Clayfield Associates Ltd would subscribe to the CBs which were placed by Kingsway SW Securities Ltd.

CCT said the CBs carried the right to convert either in whole or in part into CCT shares at an initial conversion price of HK$0.36 a share, subject to adjustment, in denominations of not less than HK$10,000.

The conversion price represented a discount of about 11.98 percent to the average closing price of CCT shares for the last five trading days to April 2, and a 6.49 percent discount to CCT's April 2 close, it said.
The bonds, which mature on April 6, 1999, carry a coupon of seven percent annually paid quarterly, CCT said.
If fully converted, CCT would issue 240 million conversion shares, representing 17.38 percent of existing capital, and 14.81 percent of CCT's enlarged capital, it said.
It said the equity stake in CCT of major shareholder Billboss Assets Ltd, controlled by CCT chairman Clement Shiu Tong-mak, would fall to 27.71 percent from 32.52 percent, assuming full conversion.
CCT said it had applied for trading in its shares to resume on Tuesday, after being suspended from April 3.
